ticket.title: storypole cannot find its store from a git worktree
ticket.description:
Found by the SP-35 two-client test. storypole resolves its store by walking ancestors for .gaugeblock/storypole or .storypole, which cannot see a linked worktree: a worktree is a sibling directory, so the walk finds nothing above it and the command either fails or builds a second store. GaugeblockPaths::discover does the right thing (it resolves through the git common dir), and ADR 0001 rests on exactly that property, but store_locate does not consult it. Evidence from the test: eight concurrent storypole update calls, four run from the worktree checkout, returned Task not found for a ticket that exists - the four that ran from the main checkout succeeded. This is the load-bearing gap for parallel agent work: until the store follows the common dir, two agents in two worktrees are not working on one store.

CORRECTED 2026-11-08, after measuring instead of theorising.

The symptom was real; the cause was not what this ticket said. A linked worktree carries its own copies of
tracked files - measured: ledger.jsonl has different inodes in main (56762556) and in agent-b (56762621) -
so .gaugeblock/storypole is checked out per branch and the ancestor walk correctly found the worktree's own
copy. It reported Task not found because that copy held a ledger with no tickets: the tickets were created
on another branch after the commit the worktree was cut from.

So the failure was ADR 0009 working as intended (tracked source follows the branch), not a resolution bug.

The genuine gap, which IS fixed (f05a136): when a checkout has no local .gaugeblock at all, the ancestor walk
either failed or built a second store. Resolution now consults the git common dir, after the caller's own
store and before the suite fallback, and accepts it only when it is the same repository.

WHAT THIS TICKET SHOULD NOW OWN: the derived layer still resolves to the working tree instead of the common
dir. Two worktrees therefore keep two index.sqlite files and would keep two lease registries, which is
wasteful for the index and wrong for leases - a claim in one worktree must be visible in the other before any
merge. That is SP-39's requirement arriving from a different direction, and the two should be decided
once: derived state resolves through the common dir, tracked state follows the branch.

TRIAGED 2026-11-12, and this P1 is not a live regression - but it is not closeable either, and the reason is a decision rather than code.

The shipped defect in it was fixed: a checkout with no local .gaugeblock now resolves through the git common dir (f05a136), and the worktree symptom it was filed from was ADR 0009 working as intended - tracked state follows the branch, so a worktree cut before the tickets were created legitimately holds a ledger without them.

What remains is the last paragraph of the description: the derived layer (index.sqlite, and the lease registry when it exists) still resolves to the working tree, so two worktrees keep two indexes and would keep two lease registries - a claim in one worktree invisible in the other until a merge. That is SP-39 arriving from another direction, and it cannot be decided per-ticket: derived state through the common dir, tracked state following the branch, decided once.

RECOMMENDATION, for whoever takes it: fix the split as a single change with SP-39 - derived paths resolve via the common dir, tracked paths keep the ancestor walk - and add the test that two worktrees of one repository share one lease registry and one index while keeping their own ticket files. Until that decision is made this ticket is a design fork, not a bug to patch, and I have left it open rather than closing it on the half that was already fixed.

CLOSED 2026-11-12 as DESIGNED, per an explicit decision, with the invariant written down (storypole feb3fbb; verified on the storypole chain, exit 0).

WHAT THE TICKET GOT WRONG, measured: it said two worktrees "would keep two lease registries". Leases have lived in the git common dir since GB-333 (leases/mod.rs:45), beside the ticket numbers (ticket_keys.rs:38), and a_lease_taken_in_one_checkout_blocks_the_other (storypole-cli tests/two_client_records_tests.rs:114) already proves a claim in one checkout blocks the other. The correctness property the P1 was worried about has been true and tested for some time.

WHAT IS LEFT, and why it stays that way: only index.sqlite is per-worktree. Sharing it was considered and rejected - it indexes TRACKED source, which follows the branch by design, so one index serving two worktrees would describe a tree one of them is not standing in. A cache that answers for the wrong branch is worse than a cache that is rebuilt.

The rule now lives in ARCHITECTURE 2.1 rather than in this ticket, which is the durable half: tracked state follows the branch, shared facts (leases, numbers) live in the git common dir, and caches follow what they cache.
